name: Efficient
rationale: Dialysis for oliguric AKI; confirm intravascular haemolysis with a poor marrow response; exclude TMA (no fragments, ADAMTS13 53%) and rhabdomyolysis (CK 33); kidney biopsy; ask again about the urine; high-sensitivity flow cytometry. The case must show: dark urine now and, only on a specific question, recurring episodes since 2016; haemoglobinuria (blood 2+ with few red cells); haemoglobin casts and tubular haemosiderin on biopsy; the granulocyte clone of 98.46%.

name: Warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
rationale: DAT positive for IgG and C3d; the team started methylprednisolone. The case must show: no spherocytes; a non-reactive eluate; low reticulocytes, which fit marrow involvement better than AIHA; escalation of immunosuppression (rituximab, splenectomy) is a must-not-do.

name: Normal conventional CD55/CD59 flow cytometry
rationale: The conventional assay on day 12 was normal after four units of washed red cells. The case must show: red cell acetylcholinesterase only slightly low; the conventional result is normal whenever it is ordered; the high-sensitivity result is clearly positive in granulocytes; accepting the conventional result as excluding the diagnosis is a must-not-do.

name: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TTP, HUS, complement-mediated HUS, HIT)
rationale: Haemolysis, AKI, falling platelets and loose stools. The case must show: no schistocytes; ADAMTS13 53.2%; stool culture negative; C3 normal; HIT antibody negative; plasma exchange is a must-not-do.

name: Rhabdomyolysis or myoglobinuria
rationale: Dark urine with dipstick blood and AKI. The case must show: CK 33 U/L; no urine myoglobin; no muscle symptoms.

name: Glomerulonephritis, lupus or vasculitis
rationale: AKI with haematuria on dipstick and proteinuria. The case must show: ANA, anti-dsDNA and ANCA negative (article); anti-GBM negative; no red cell casts; glomeruli normal on biopsy.

name: Myeloma cast nephropathy
rationale: AKI, anaemia and casts in a 60-year-old. The case must show: no paraprotein; polyclonal light chains with a normal ratio; low (not high) calcium; haemoglobin, not light-chain, casts.

name: Infection after influenza (sepsis, leptospirosis, malaria, dengue)
rationale: AKI after a febrile illness with loose stools. The case must show: afebrile; procalcitonin normal; cultures and tropical serology negative.

name: Marrow failure (aplastic anaemia, myelodysplasia)
rationale: Low reticulocytes and falling platelets. The case must show: marrow mildly hypocellular without dysplasia or excess blasts; normal karyotype, FISH and myeloid panel; marrow flow shows the GPI-linked antigen loss (R06).

name: Venous thrombosis and its causes
rationale: D-dimer 8.82 mg/L; intrarenal venous thrombi on biopsy; right iliac vein thrombosis. The case must show: thrombophilia screen, lupus anticoagulant and HIT antibody negative; renal veins patent on Doppler; the post-biopsy haematoma delays full anticoagulation.

name: Other effects of severe kidney failure
rationale: A player working up the AKI may order renal and metabolic tests. The case must show: raised osmolality, PTH and natriuretic peptides; tubular urine indices; proteinuria consistent with the uPCR; low-normal HbA1c; enlarged kidneys without obstruction on CT.

name: Gastrointestinal cause of the loose stools
rationale: Loose watery stools after influenza. The case must show: soft non-tender abdomen; liver tests, amylase and lipase unremarkable apart from renal effects; stool culture negative; normal abdominal ultrasound apart from the kidneys.
